Generic AI can process language. Insurance execution requires context. mea Ora, mea’s proprietary insurance AI, is built on the industry’s only insurance domain-specific language model SM and the industry’s only insurance knowledge graph SM . That’s what an insurance knowledge graph does in practice. It understands the work before the work starts. It knows: The difference between a bordereaux, a statement of account, and a premium finance agreement CAT XOL is a treaty structure FNOL triggers a claims workflow That a Schedule of Values is structured data, not free text, whatever format it arrives in That missing attachment points and net retained lines are red flags, not optional fields Private learning architecture Insurance-native from day one. Private learning by design. mea arrives pre-trained on the language, documents and workflows of insurance. It then adapts to how your organization works, inside your own instance, with data that stays private to you. 01 Pre-trained for insurance mea already understands insurance language, documents, entities and workflows before it reaches you. Nothing starts from zero. 02 Adapted to your guidelines It takes on your terminology, schemas, operating procedures, appetite rules and workflows; all specific to how your business runs. 03 Improved through governed feedback Corrections and approvals from your team refine your configuration, with every change reviewed and versioned. 04 Learning stays private Each client operates on its own instance. Your data is your data, and the learning derived from it is private to you. Generic models improve by pooling everyone’s data. mea arrives already knowing insurance, then sharpens inside your instance on your work alone. FAQs Do we have to replace our existing systems? No. mea runs behind the systems you already use. Start with one workflow, keep your current stack, and expand where it pays. Where you would rather replace a core system, mea can run the full stack instead. Is this another interface for our teams to learn? No. mea does the work behind your existing systems. Where an interface helps, it is built around the workflow and the people using it. Is mea generic AI configured for insurance? No. General-purpose LLMs are trained broadly on public data and need training on insurance specifics before they can be trusted with the work: the documents, the terminology, the rules and the relationships between them. mea starts from the other side. mea Ora runs on the industry's only insurance domain-specific language model (dsLM) and the industry's only insurance knowledge graph, trained on five years of real (re)insurance workflows, documents and decisions, with 125,000+ pre-trained insurance fields available out of the box. It knows the work before the work starts. Why can mea do this when others cannot? Executing a workflow end to end takes three things at once: insurance-native AI that reads the complex end of the market, an execution engine proven at operations scale, and a decision environment underwriters trust. Each takes years alone, and every other class of competitor is missing at least one. The difference shows up in what arrives at the end. Most AI produces a suggestion and hands it back to a person to action, while mea's agents clear the submission, triage it against appetite, validate the data, populate the connected system, flag blockers with a guided resolution, and log every action for audit. We already use an AI provider. Does mea conflict with that? No. The insurance intelligence in mea Ora is mea's own, and it works interchangeably with leading general LLMs. Where a general model adds value, mea works with the provider you have standardized on, inside the agreements and controls you already have in place. Your model choice stays yours. How does mea impact the bottom line? mea removes operating work, applies your rules consistently, and returns capacity to your expert teams. For carriers that lands in the combined ratio. For MGAs, more GWP without added headcount. For brokers, higher productivity and margin. In a demo, mea models the impact against your own book and workflow. Do we need to fix everything at once? No. mea is modular, and the modules are layers of one system rather than separate products. Start with mea Operations in the workflow with the clearest ROI, then extend across the others as the value proves out.
